newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly gain again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly gain again.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly moved up slightly again Wednesday in lackluster trade, helped by stable crude and some Florida utility and bunker interest, industry sources said.

"High sulphur in the Gulf is pretty tight and there has been some forward low sulphur interest, so I don't see fuel prices falling back much," said one cash trader, noting East Coast generation demand remained slack due to mild weather.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent again edged up slightly to $15.50-75 a barrel, with June paper also modestly higher in the $16.25-50 area, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour held steady at $16.25, traders said.
New York high sulphurs were unchanged to 10 cents higher, with 2.2 percent now talked at $14.40-65.
U.S. Gulf, three percent firmed a quarter to $14.25-50 on tight supplies in the region and relatively firm bunkers.
USG one percent inched up a dime to the high-$14s.

Traders said a Florida utility may reject all offers for its one percent tender for 250,000 barrels per month from July-September. Another Florida utility reissued its tender for 60-180,000 barrels of one to three percent material for delivery prior to June 15. Bids are due Thursday at 1000 EDT.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices edged up a couple of cents Wednesday to the low-to-mid $2.40s/mmBtu, or about $15.37 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained a few cents to the low-$2.20s/mmBtu, or $13.99 a barrel.
